Two calls, not n: two is the minimum that distinguishes standing from one-shot, and it is the exact cardinality the production caller exhibits (start_alloc binds leg-F then leg-C). A .take()-instead-of-clone regression would make the second call take the Ok arm — which for bind_transparent would additionally drag a REAL socket bind into the default lane.

S-MIF-08 — with a fault armed on each of the three slots, `clear_faults()` restores both install steps to their Ok arms (each hands back a guard), and a SECOND `clear_faults()` on the already-disarmed double changes nothing and does not fail. FAULT ARMS ARE PURE — an armed fault short-circuits BEFORE any syscall, so all four scenarios perform ZERO I/O and belong in the default lane. The Ok arm of bind_transparent binds a REAL, PLAIN (non-IP_TRANSPARENT) loopback listener because there is no way to fabricate a std::net::TcpListener without a syscall and the worker's Ok path consumes a live listener it accepts on; the Ok arm of the two installs returns the INERT guard whose Drop is a no-op. THE FIVE ORDINARY CALL SITES ARE BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING BY CONSTRUCTION, and the hoist is REQUIRED not stylistic. Each passes a value byte-identical to today's `timestamp_for(tick, node_id)`: `fail_closed_on_netns_provision` `:516` → `timestamp_for(tick, node_id.clone())`; `FinalizeFailed` `:1065` → `timestamp_for(tick, prior_row.node_id.clone())`; `StartAllocation` `:1239` → `timestamp_for(tick, node_id.clone())`; `RestartAllocation` `:1457` → `timestamp_for(tick, prior_row.node_id.clone())`; `StopAllocation` `:1566` → `timestamp_for(tick, prior_row.node_id.clone())`.
